lots.key_photo_findings: I enlarged the stone. It is translucent milky-crystal body with play of colour in vertical columns or streaks (blue, green, some red and orange) and a yellowish-straw rim on the lower edge. That columnar or 'digit' pattern and the straw body tone are typical of Ethiopian (Welo) hydrophane opal, not Australian jelly or crystal opal. This is my judgement from one photo, not confirmed. No cracks visible. Size estimated from the jar: roughly 10 x 8 mm cabochon, which fits about 2 to 3 ct if it is domed.
lots.condition: Appears clean with no visible crazing or chips in one top-down photo. The back and the thickness are not shown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the opal Australian or Ethiopian (Welo)? Has the 3 ct weight been checked on a scale, and are there any certificates or a vendor note? Can you confirm there is no crazing, and say what the back looks like?
lots.score_reason: If it is Ethiopian, a 3 ct stone like this is probably a $30 to $80 item. If it is Australian crystal opal it could be worth more, but the photo points the other way.
